Seminar Title:

Experimental Investigation of the Thermal Performance of PCM-Integrated Fly Ash Bricks Using Sustainable Shell Materials

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Mechanical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Shovit Kumar Sahu ( Rollno : 523me1002)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

ME-001 (Seminar Room)

Date and Time:

28 Oct 2026 3:30 PM

Contact:

Sushil Kumar Rathore

Abstract:

The integration of phase change materials (PCMs) into building envelopes offers an effective approach to passive thermal regulation. However, limited research has explored the thermal performance of PCM capsules fabricated using natural materials and industrial by-products. This study experimentally investigates macroencapsulated OM35 PCM-integrated fly ash bricks using three sustainable shell compositions: red mud&ndashgypsum, bottom ash&ndashbentonite, and Visakhapatnam red sand&ndashbentonite. The thermal properties of OM35 were characterized through differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), which yielded a melting enthalpy of 166.1 J/g. Four brick specimens were fabricated, comprising one reference brick without PCM and three PCM-integrated bricks, each containing approximately 146 g of PCM. Their thermal performance was evaluated under outdoor climatic conditions in Jodhpur, India, over three consecutive days using peak temperature reduction, thermal amplitude, decrement factor, and thermal response during PCM melting and solidification as performance indicators. In addition, compressive strength testing was performed to assess the mechanical performance of the fabricated bricks and their suitability for building applications. Among the PCM-integrated bricks, the Visakhapatnam red sand brick (VRSB) demonstrated superior thermal performance, achieving a peak temperature reduction of 4.54 &degC (10.30%) and a thermal amplitude reduction of 39.85% compared with the reference brick. It also exhibited the lowest decrement factor of 0.46, the maximum time lag of 135 min, and a compressive strength of 9.64 MPa. These findings demonstrate the potential of Visakhapatnam red sand as a sustainable capsule shell material for PCM-integrated fly ash bricks and their application in passive thermal regulation of buildings.
